question.questionText: We've discovered this great café and we _______ there a lot.
question.explanationHtml:
Detailed Explanation:
The blank requires a verb tense that matches the context of the sentence. The sentence 'We've discovered this great café and we _______ there a lot.' uses 'We've discovered' (present perfect), indicating a recent discovery with a present result. The second part describes an action that started in the past and continues to the present (frequent visits to the café). The present perfect continuous tense ('have been going') is used to express an action that began in the past and is still happening now, especially with repeated actions.
  • has been going (verb phrase): 'Has been going' is present perfect continuous but used with singular third person subjects (he/she/it), not with 'we'.
  • have been going (verb phrase): 'Have been going' is present perfect continuous, used with plural subjects like 'we', indicating an action that started in the past and continues to the present.
  • had been going (verb phrase): 'Had been going' is past perfect continuous, used for actions that were ongoing in the past before another past event. It does not fit the present context.
  • will have been going (verb phrase): 'Will have been going' is future perfect continuous, used for actions that will be ongoing up to a point in the future. It does not fit the context.
Related structure or vocabulary: Present perfect continuous tense: have/has been + V-ing. Used to describe actions that started in the past and continue to the present, often with repeated actions.

  • have been doing (verb phrase): Present perfect continuous tense but with 'have' instead of 'has.' 'Sandy' is a singular subject, so 'has' is required.

  • have been doing (cụm động từ): Thì hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn nhưng dùng 'have' thay vì 'has.' 'Sandy' là chủ ngữ số ít nên phải dùng 'has.'
